title: Founding Engineer (Fullstack JS)
company: Unimatch Lab is an AI-driven venture studio — not a single product and not a classical IT company with one linear trajectory. Several directions run in parallel, from consumer hardware to B2B platforms. The stated goal is to be among the top 50 AI companies worldwide, with $10B in combined asset value by 2032. The studio is OKR-driven and runs on measurable results, speed, transparency and ownership. There are two blocks. Government is the first revenue-generating direction: an AI-agentic ecosystem for the UAE public sector — process automation, document workflows, services for citizens and business. Venture is the classic studio model: fast MVPs and hypothesis testing. Products in flight include Neybo, an AI hardware toy for the US kids market; Cortex and Future Fork, a B2B module family covering HR, legal, finance and planning; a wellness product aggregating health data behind an AI agent, currently a proof of concept; and a gamified language-learning platform. The principle is the same everywhere: build it for ourselves first, then take it outside.
role: Founding Engineer (Fullstack JS) — the owner of one AI-native application end to end, effectively its CTO from day one. Fully remote, full time, paid as an individual contractor.
pitch: The CEO or CPO sets the goals, the KPIs and the product frame, and hands over a clickable proof of concept. Execution, timelines and the technical result are yours: you take that prototype to an MVP in production and keep going. Four areas run through every stage — architecture and technical decisions, where you are the final call within the product; code quality and engineering standards, including review process, testing strategy and CI/CD with safe rollback; engineering velocity through automation, where anything that can be delegated to an agent is; and the engineering knowledge system of ADRs, guidelines and onboarding material. Working with AI agents and vibe-coding — Cursor, agent pipelines — is part of the daily process rather than an experiment. There are boundaries: product decomposition and feature prioritisation sit with the PM, deep infrastructure and security with the Head of Infra, and marketing and sales join after the MVP. In the first weeks you build a 30-60-90 plan together and commit to delivery.

faq.q: compensation and how it is structured
faq.a: The rate for this role is around $6,000 a month. The structure is base plus ship-bonuses, quarterly or monthly, with targets agreed in your first weeks. Equity and revenue share come in once the product generates revenue, with details in a term sheet after the first month.

Payments currently go out in crypto, and it is done properly: company wallet, invoice, AML checks, wallet rotation, and custodial rather than exchange wallets. You work as an individual contractor, so taxes are on your side. By the end of 2026 the company moves to fiat B2B payments through a bank or a Deel-like platform; roughly the next three months are still crypto. If you need help legalising it in your jurisdiction, a lawyer is brought in.

An AI-driven venture studio running several directions in parallel: a government block building an AI-agentic ecosystem for the UAE public sector, and a venture block doing fast MVPs across consumer and B2B products.

faq.q: which product or stream this role belongs to
faq.a: The specific stream is discussed separately at a later stage. At this point what matters is the overall portfolio picture.

faq.q: what the role owns and what it does not
faq.a: You own architecture and technical decisions, code quality and engineering standards, engineering velocity, and the engineering knowledge system. You do not own product decomposition and feature prioritisation — that is the PM — nor deep infrastructure and security, which sit with the Head of Infra.
Node.js and React, with Next.js, React Native, GraphQL, REST and WebSockets, OAuth2 and JWT. LangChain and LangGraph on the AI side, OpenTelemetry for observability.

faq.q: working hours, remote work and time zones
faq.a: Fully remote with a flexible schedule outside core time. Work runs in two-week sprints — planning, delivery, retro. Sync with the US matters for this role: both coasts, with core-time windows when everyone is reachable.

faq.q: the team and who you would work with
faq.a: Directly with the CEO or CPO, the Head of Infra, and the Head of Ops on a dotted line for OKRs and process. After the MVP, marketing, growth partners and ops join. Across the studio there are other Founding Engineers for architecture review when your decisions touch shared infrastructure.
The team is becoming international and the company is moving to international hiring, so English is critically important in daily work. The bar for this role is B2 or above.

faq.q: the hiring process and what happens next
faq.a: This screening, then conversations with the team, and a portfolio with code samples is expected. Before the next stages it is worth reading the operating manual at working-with-nick.vercel.app — it exists so both sides can make a deliberate decision.

Five or more years as a full-stack JS engineer with a backend focus, regular use of AI coding tools such as Cursor, product thinking and scope management, and production experience with releases and incidents.
